questions.prompt: What problem did a unified architecture solve for graphics?
options: Load imbalance: separate vertex and pixel units sat idle when a scene was lopsided
questions.explanation: One pool of processors runs whatever kind of work the frame needs.

questions.prompt: An SM has 8 SP lanes and warps of 32 threads. How many cycles does one warp instruction occupy the lanes?
With 8,192 registers and 768 resident threads per SM, what's the most registers each thread can use at full occupancy?
Which ideas from this paper are still central to GPUs today?
options: The SM as a multithreaded core
Warps of 32 threads and SIMT execution
Blocks that share on-chip memory and synchronise with barriers
questions.explanation: Separate vertex and pixel processors is exactly what the paper replaced.

questions.prompt: Why does the paper's model make the same program run on GPUs with different numbers of SMs?
options: Blocks are independent and can be scheduled onto however many SMs exist
Every GPU has the same number of SMs
questions.explanation: Independent blocks let hardware scale: more SMs means more blocks at once (fewer waves).
